review_scope: Independent source and assertion review for guest EXT-F-1003 T04 and T10; no native run, build, or inventory changes.

verdict_a_behavior_and_spec.T04: Candidate now checks selected and stored value, theme class, and body background against resolved --background in warm and panel-document-reload observations. This strengthens applied-appearance evidence. It does not show the extension was fully reloaded/reopened or prove the visible side-panel surface by screenshot; canonical T04 therefore remains partial until native evidence closes those gaps.
verdict_a_behavior_and_spec.T10: Candidate selects each Ask/Act value, panel-reloads, then opens Chat, clicks New chat, and requires the mode label and icon to match. This exercises the consumer UI. It does not send a first action or assert a server payload, and it does not cover full extension reload; retain those gaps.
verdict_a_behavior_and_spec.scope: These are acceptance-driver changes, not application behavior fixes. Current candidate has no native acceptance receipt, so neither outcome is proven for the installed extension.

verdict_b_quality.assertions: The theme and chat predicates reject wrong rendered-background flag, wrong mode label/icon, missing new-chat control, and inactive chat. Runtime observations use a unique active pane and allowlisted preference values; new-chat waits for the combined expected UI state.
verdict_b_quality.automation: The focused helper test is listed in package.json test:focused-acceptance. Independently ran node --test tests/browser/settings-guest-preference-batch.test.mjs: 2 passed, 0 failed. No browser/native/build run was made.
verdict_b_quality.data_scope: Observed fields are fixed labels, allowlisted values, booleans, and counts; raw settings state is not returned. The appearance probe is appended hidden and removed immediately.

not_run: No local browser, heavy test, build, extension reload, server action, native dispatch, or inventory mutation.
